Lessons.Title: Scaling the Inputs
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Calculate the scale factor $k$ needed to transform the input of a function to fit a situation. Describe (orally and in writing) the effect of a scale factor on the input of a function.
The transformation g(x)=f(kx) compresses the graph horizontally by factor 1/|k| if |k|>1, with an additional y-axis reflection when k<0. It does not multiply output directly.

Practice Problem 3: A bacteria population, in thousands, is modeled by the function \(f(d) = 30 \boldcdot 2^d\) where \(d\) is the number of days since it was first measured. The function \(g\) gives the bacteria population, in thousands, \(w\) weeks after it was first measured. Express \(g\) in terms of \(f\). Explain your reasoning. Practice Problem 5: Here is the graph of a function \(f\). Reflecting \(f\) across the \(x\)-axis and then across the vertical line \(y=1\) takes the graph of \(f\) back to itself. Tyler says that this means \(f\) is an odd function. Do you agree with Tyler? Explain your reasoning. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: The population of sloths in an area has been increasing by 5% each year since 2000. Let \(P\) model the population \(P(t)\), in thousands, of sloths \(t\) years after the year 2000. The graph of \(p(t) = 1.05^t\) has a general shape that fits the data. Find a scale factor \(k\) so that \(P(t) = kp(t)\) fits the data. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

KeyConcepts.Title: Scaling inputs
KeyConcepts.Definition: The transformation g(x)=f(kx) compresses the graph horizontally by factor 1/|k| if |k|>1, with an additional y-axis reflection when k<0. It does not multiply output directly.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Apply the exact task conditions, mathematical operation, and permitted domain.
KeyConcepts.Example: Given f(x)=x², express g(x)=f(2x) and describe the change. Answer: g(x)=4x²; horizontal compression by factor1/2.
